data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman family name Caesar. Caesarius is a Latin name meaning 'Caesar's man'. This name was popular among early Christians, with St. Caesarius of Arles being a notable bearer. The name Caesarius carries the meaning “Caesar's man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Caesarius usually hope their child will grow to embody caesar's man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Servant of Caesar, symbolizing dedication and loyalty.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Caesarius total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: קיזריוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם קיזריוס נובע מהמונח kaisar, שפירושו 'קיסר' או 'מנהיג'. השם קשור לשושלת הקיסרית, שהייתה משפחת מלכים רומאית, ולכן השם נוצר לפני הבסלאבים. השם הועבר ליוונית כ-Καισαρίω, ולפיכך, השם היווני קיזריוס הוא גם נפוץ. השם קיזריוס קשור גם למסורת הנוצרית, כאשר הקדוש Caesarius היה בישוף ואיש דת ידוע.

in_greek.name: Καισαρίω
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όνομα Καισαρίω προέρχεται από τον όρο Kαισαρ, ο οποίος σημαίνει «Καισαρ» ή «αρχηγός». Το όνομα συνδέεται με τη δυναστεία των Καισαρ, μιας ρωμαϊκής βασιλικής οικογένειας, και έτσι το όνομα δημιουργήθηκε πριν από τους Σλάβους. Το όνομα μεταφράστηκε στη γαλλική ως Caesarius, και έτσι το γαλλικό όνομα Caesarius απαντάται επίσης. Το όνομα Καισαρίω απαντάται επίσης στην ελληνική, και συνδέεται επίσης με την ιστορία της Εκκλησίας, καθώς ο άγιος Caesarius ήταν επίσκοπος και προστάτης της Εκκλησίας.

in_english.name: Caesarius
in_english.meaning: son of Caesar, Roman emperor or ruler
in_english.long_meaning: The name Caesarius originates from the Latin word Caesare, meaning 'Caesar' or 'leader'. The name is linked to the Caesarean dynasty, a Roman royal family, and thus the name was created before the Slavs. The name Caesarius is also found in French, and is associated with Christian tradition, as Saint Caesarius was a bishop and a patron of the Church. Caesarius is also a name found in the Bible, as it is mentioned in the Book of Revelation, chapter 17, verse 10, as a title for the Antichrist. In modern times, the name Caesarius is used by some Christians as a name for their children, as it is seen as a strong and powerful name, associated with leadership and authority.

data.cultural_impact: Caesarius was a common name among the Latin-speaking populations in the Roman Empire, and its adoption by early Christians highlighted the relationship between Christianity and the Roman civilization. This blending of the Roman and Christian worlds is a significant aspect of the history of European Christianity, and the name Caesarius serves as a reminder of this cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian tradition, Caesarius is the name of several saints, and its spiritual significance lies in the fact that it honors the faith and dedication of those who remained devoted to God in the midst of the secular world. The name Caesarius thus represents a call to live a life of faithfulness and service to God, even in the midst of the business and obligations of the world. It is a reminder that one's commitment to God should never be compromised, even in the face of secular pressures.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Caesarius, meaning 'venerable Caesar,' embodies the fusion of spiritual piety and secular power. It invokes the caesura in one's life, signifying a pause for reflection and devotion amidst worldly responsibilities.

historical_references.reference: Caesarius of Arles was a famous bishop who lived around 470-542 AD. He is known for his role in the spread of Christianity in the Gauls (France) during the 5th and 6th centuries.
historical_references.context: Caesarius played a significant role in the conversion of the Visigoths and other Germanic tribes to Christianity. He founded numerous monasteries and schools, and his rule for monks, the Regula, became a model for monastic life in the Western Church.

historical_references.reference: Saint Caesarius of Bordeaux was a bishop and martyr who lived around 337 AD. He is often considered as the first bishop of Bordeaux and was martyred during the persecution of Christians under the Roman Emperor Constantine I.
historical_references.context: Caesarius was born in Bordeaux and was a prominent figure in the city's Christian community. He was arrested and put on trial for his faith, and was ultimately executed. His relics were later discovered and venerated, and a basilica was built in his honor in the city.
